entities.summary:
AB Volvo, founded in 1927 in Gothenburg, Sweden, is the world's second-largest manufacturer of heavy trucks, buses, and construction equipment (with operations separate from Volvo Cars, which was sold to Ford in 1999 and to Geely in 2010). Volvo Trucks, Buses, and Construction Equipment generate over €45 billion in annual revenues. Volvo's contribution to automotive safety — the three-point safety belt invented by Nils Bohlin in 1959, which Volvo made freely available to all car manufacturers — has saved an estimated one million lives.

Volvo was founded by Assar Gabrielsson and Gustaf Larson as an automobile company with the Swedish slogan 'Volvo — it rolls' (from the Latin 'volvere'). The three-point safety belt invention by Bohlin in 1959, and Volvo's unprecedented decision to share the patent with all automakers rather than keep it exclusive, is one of history's most consequential acts of corporate altruism — estimated to have saved over a million lives since 1959.

Volvo Cars was sold separately: Ford acquired it in 1999 for $6.45 billion; Geely of China acquired it from Ford in 2010 for $1.8 billion — one of the great automotive bargains following the 2008 crisis. AB Volvo (the trucks/buses/construction equipment company) remained Swedish-listed. Volvo's 2020s electrification push — committing to sell only electric Volvo trucks in Europe by 2030 — represents the Swedish industrial tradition of combining environmental responsibility with engineering excellence.
